keywords: newton newtons motion force forces inertia acceleration mass action reaction momentum friction
facts: First law: an object stays at rest or keeps moving at constant velocity unless a net force acts (inertia).
Second law: F = m × a; force in newtons, mass in kg, acceleration in m/s².
Third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
Net force is the sum of all forces; friction opposes motion.

narration.text: Isaac Newton described three simple rules for how things move.
First law: an object stays still or keeps moving unless a force acts on it.
Second law: force equals mass times acceleration.
Third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
The rocket engine pushes hot gas downward.
The gas pushes the rocket upward with an equal force. That is the third law.
The upward force is bigger than its weight, so it speeds up.

scenes.heading: Step 3: Using F = m × a
scenes.problem: A 2 kg ball is pushed with a 10 N force. Find its acceleration.

narration.text: Rearrange the second law: acceleration equals force divided by mass.
Put in ten newtons and two kilograms.
The ball speeds up by five metres per second, every second.

scenes.heading: Step 3: Net force with friction
scenes.problem: A 1,000 kg car: 3,000 N engine force, 1,000 N friction. Find a.

narration.text: Friction pushes backwards, so subtract it: the net force is two thousand newtons.
Divide the net force by the mass of one thousand kilograms.
The car accelerates at two metres per second squared.
If the forces were equal, the net force would be zero and speed would stay constant.

scenes.heading: Step 9: Common mistake: action and reaction

narration.text: When you push a wall, the wall pushes back on you.
The two forces are equal in size and opposite in direction.
They act on different objects, so they do not cancel each other out.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.question: A ball rolls on a smooth, flat floor. Why does it keep moving?
options: Inertia: almost no force stops it

narration.text: Quick check. Why does a ball keep rolling on a smooth floor?
Inertia. With almost no force to stop it, it keeps moving.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.question: The same force pushes a 1 kg cart and a 4 kg cart. Which accelerates more?

narration.text: Quick check. Which cart speeds up more?
The one kilogram cart. Less mass means more acceleration for the same force.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.question: If the net force on a moving object is zero, it will…

narration.text: Quick check. What happens when the net force is zero?
It keeps moving at a constant velocity. That is the first law.
